incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II: Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL) and R.223-1 to R.223-12 (incorporation formalities); Articles R.123-1 to R.123-166 (RNE registration); implementing Decree No. 2024-484 and the Order of 14 November 2023 on the Guichet unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by the INPI, transmitting to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association), Declaration of Compliance (Déclaration de conformité), and Declaration of Subscription and Payment of Capital (Déclaration de souscription et de versement du capital), submitted electronically via the Guichet unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SARL; the capital is freely fixed in the Articles and fully subscribed by the shareholders. Cash contributions must be paid up to at least 20% at incorporation, the balance within 5 years (Art. L.223-7 C. com.). The funds must be escrowed and blocked in a bank account or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations and released only upon RNE registration, evidenced by the banker's blocked-funds certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: THE UNDERSIGNED FOUNDING SHAREHOLDERS, acting as the constitutive general meeting of (Company Name), RESOLVE: FIRST, the draft Articles of Association are adopted. SECOND, the share capital of [EUR X] is subscribed in full and the contribution funds are deposited pursuant to a bank blocked-account certificate. THIRD, the registered office is fixed at [address] within the jurisdiction of the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce de [City]. FOURTH, [Name] is appointed Gérant for an indefinite term, with full corporate powers. FIFTH, the Gérant is authorized to sign the Declaration of Compliance, place legal announcements, and complete all filings with the Guichet unique and the RNE. SIXTH, formation costs and expenses are approved and ratified.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) for corporate income tax and VAT; Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) with the DELTA/GUN single window for export clearance and exporter/EORI status. Official portals: impots.gouv.fr, formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet Unique des formalités d'entreprises), douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SARL, formation is achieved through the Guichet Unique administered by the INPI, and the formalities automatically generate a SIREN/SIRET registration. The SIE then issues the intra-EU VAT identifier (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire) formatted FR followed by two digits and the nine-character local key; no separate SIREN application is required for non-resident shareholders. For export operations, the SARL must obtain an EORI number for customs declarations in DELTA, register its exporter status and risk profile with DGDDI, and maintain an active bank account in France for FX repatriation. A foreign seller not established in France but supplying French customers may apply directly for French VAT registration through the normal SIE procedure or appoint a fiscal representative where required; however, the existing resident SARL should execute all registrations as a French established entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. A standard SARL is taxable at entity level under corporate income tax (IS) as the default classification. Election for pass-through tax at the level of individual shareholders (IR) is available only to qualified family SARLs under Articles 239 AA/239 AAA CGI and must be exercised within the statutory filing deadline of the first fiscal year. Anti-hybrid and branch mismatch elections under ATAD are administered by treaty/residence analysis rather than domestic elections; a French VAT grouping election (assujetti unique) is available under Articles 256 C III CGI for closely connected persons. Fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) election for corporate income tax is limited to groups holding at least 95% equity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA – Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 — France requires VAT registration as soon as an independent economic activity is exercised in French territory; there is no numeric turnover threshold for B2B agricultural trading. The small-enterprise franchise (art. 293 B CGI) nominally exempts goods sellers up to EUR 85,000 and service providers up to EUR 37,500, but is generally unreliable for a fully structured SARL conducting bulk grain transactions; the EU distance-selling OSS threshold of EUR 10,000 is likewise inapplicable to export bulk commodity flows.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing applies to all domestic B2B VAT invoices in France from 1 September 2026 (large and mid-size taxpayers) and 1 September 2027 (small taxpayers) under the 2024 Finance Act. Invoices must be transmitted via the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or a registered Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP), in Factur-X / EN 16931 or CII formats, with transactional e-reporting for cross-border and B2C transactions. France is not a real-time state-clearance jurisdiction (no digital digital-stamping such as in Italy); however, every export declaration must be electronically validated through the DGDDI DELTA/GUN single window, which applies continuous customs risk scoring and, for qualifying traders, AEO status.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating of exports under Article 262-II-1° CGI is granted for definitive shipments of physical goods transported directly out of France into a third country, provided the sale is properly evidenced, the goods physically leave the customs territory, and the DGDDI accepts the export declaration. Intra-EU supplies of grain and corn are treated as exempt intra-Community deliveries only if the EU customer VAT ID is valid and the recapitulative statement (DEB) is filed. Offshore services directly linked to the exported bulk goods may also qualify for 0%. The burden of proof is on the SARL to demonstrate departure, transport continuity, and payment repatriation; mere issuance of invoices or bill of lading without customs validation is insufficient.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAE) electronically validated in the DGDDI DELTA/GUN single window
Bill of Lading, CMR, or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from France
Commercial Invoice and Packing List issued by the exporting SARL
Inward Remittance Certificate (justification de rapatriement) — bank credit advice or SWIFT confirmation proving payment repatriation to a French bank account
Sales contract and/or Irrevocable Transferable Letter of Credit evidencing the commercial transaction
Certificate of Origin, EUR.1, or Form A where preferential origin is claimed
Intra-Community DEB summary statement for EU-destination deliveries and EX1 attachment where required
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The French administration reverses the 0% rate and reassesses VAT at 20% when the documentary chain fails: missing customs validation, inconsistent transport data, circular delivery or payment structures, false DAE references, or absence of valid EU customer VAT ID. The tax audit (vérification de comptabilité) treats export transactions under the exploitation of cross-border risk, applying retrospective clawback over the standard three-year reprise period, extended to ten years where the company is engaged in fraudulent cross-border transactions or foreign-account concealment. Civil penalties range from 40% of the reassessed rights for deliberate bad faith (manquement délibéré) to 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres (manœuvres frauduleuses), plus monthly interest on arrears at 0.2%. Criminal prosecution under Article 1741 CGI exposes the directors to a fine of up to EUR 500,000 and five years' imprisonment for tax fraud, with the tax lien (privilège du Trésor) enforceable on corporate assets.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), acting jointly with the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) as the banking and payment-institution supervisor; exchange-control policy is co-administered with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury). France, as an EU and eurozone member, applies full liberalisation of payments and capital movements under Article 63 TFEU and Directive 88/361/EEC. There is no dedicated FX administration requiring licences, approvals, or pre-export documentation for standard agri-commodity trade flows; the Banque de France exercises only statistical balance-of-payments (BOP) monitoring.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility of the euro (EUR) for both current-account and capital-account operations. No FX licensing, no exchange allocation, and no import/export licences in the monetary sense apply to bulk grain or soybean settlements. Dividend and profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is unrestricted, subject only to French domestic withholding (generally 25% for corporate shareholders and 30% inclusive of social levies for individual non-residents) with reductions or exemptions under applicable double-tax treaties and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, plus standard CRS/FATCA reporting. Physical cash or bearer negotiable instruments of EUR 10,000 or more must be declared at the EU border under Regulation (EU) 2018/1672. BOP statistical reporting applies in two bands: (i) indirect reporting through the settling bank for all transactions, and (ii) direct monthly reporting to the Banque de France (via the FIM/CIDRE or e-BOP portals) for enterprises whose annual external transactions exceed the statutory threshold (EUR 35 million); the subject SARL, even if below the threshold, must ensure bank-mediated attribution of accurate purpose codes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. The Code Monétaire et Financier (Articles L151-1 to L165-1) imposes no mandatory repatriation, no surrender ratio, no conversion timeline, and no approved-bank requirement for export proceeds of a French SARL. The entity may freely retain USD or other currency receipts in a foreign-currency account held with a French-authorised bank, may convert into EUR at market rates at any time, and may use those proceeds directly to pay overseas suppliers or charterers. The only obligations are: (i) accurate declaration of the transaction to the reporting bank for BOP statistics; (ii) retention of underlying commercial documentation (contracts, bills of lading, invoices, LC documents) for five years under French tax and customs evidentiary rules; and (iii) compliance with EU cash declaration thresholds where physical cash is involved.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency account (EUR/USD) plus segregated Commodity Trade Finance facility for LC advising, confirmation, and discounting; optional capital escrow sub-account at incorporation

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole CIB (with the regional Caisse Régionale as the entity's principal branch under the Crédit Agricole S.A. network)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational account + agricultural export settlement account (compte de négoce céréalier) + LC/trust-receipt line tailored to grain brokerage
Operational account + structured commodity finance desk (transferable LC, bank payment obligation, trade loans), with escrow capability for vessel charter settlements
Operational account and mirror sub-accounts for freight and demurrage pass-through payments
Operational account, SME-focused KYC path, electronic banking with SWIFT connectivity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for daily treasury and small-value wires; Low for trade-finance rails. ACPR-licensed French EMIs (e.g., Qonto, Shine, Manager.one) and EU-passported challenger EMIs (Wise Business, Revolut Business) can provide EUR and USD accounts, spot FX conversion, MT103-equivalent transfers, and virtual IBAN structures. They cannot issue irrevocable documentary credits (MT700), act as confirming banks, provide banker's acceptances, discount trade bills, or issue commodity-guaranteed lines; a parallel Tier-1 relationship remains mandatory for LC-based grain settlements. Additionally, any non-French EMI must hold an ACPR licence or file a PSD2 passport notification before soliciting a French corporate client; unlicensed offshore EMIs offering USD accounts must be rejected as a compliance blocker.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permitted. ACPR guidance permits video-identification and electronic signature under Article R.561-20-2 of the Code Monétaire et Financier. In practice, Tier-1 French banks request (i) an in-person or high-grade videoconference interview with the SARL gérant (manager) and all signatories; (ii) a current Kbis extract (less than three months old) from the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés; (iii) the SARL's status/statuts with certified French translation if any annex is foreign-language; (iv) a two-document proof of registered office (lease, utility bill); and (v) for non-resident directors or shareholders, a notarised passport, apostilled proof of address, and either a banker's reference or a certified copy of the identification of the foreign parent. Physical branch attendance is not a statutory mandate but materially shortens decision time for the commodity trade finance committee; expected onboarding times are 3-8 weeks including compliance vetting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: non-resident shareholders or layered holding vehicles designed to conceal the ultimate beneficial owner(s) above the 25% statutory threshold (Articles L.561-2-2 and L.561-5 of the Code Monétaire et Financier).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kbis extract; full chain-of-title shareholder register annotated to the ultimate individuals; the statutory UBO declaration form (Formulaire UBO) filed with the Greffe; notarised passports and proof of residential address for each UBO; a signed corporate organigram by the gérant; CRS self-certifications and French taxpayer reference numbers, together with tax residence certificates (Formulaire 3558) for non-resident UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds discontinuity: initial capital is small (SARL may be formed with a low capital) yet first-month turnover reflects high-value USD LC discounting or charter-party flows, triggering suspicion of front-running or money-mule structuring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed charter party / vessel fixture note with vessel name and laycan; signed grain purchase and sale contracts (GAFTA/FOSFA terms as applicable); pro-forma and commercial invoices; draft bill of lading and vessel vetting reports; escrow agreement if funds pass through a broker's clearing account; 12-month bank statements of the contributing shareholder showing the ancestral source of funds; an audit-ready source-of-funds memorandum prepared by a French CAC (statutory auditor) once thresholds are reached.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and procurement-finance red flags: grain origin, shipping flag, charterer, or final importer touching Russia, Belarus, Syria, Iran, North Korea, or the Crimea region; EU food-related exemptions are selectively interpreted by compliance desks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Third-party vessel screening (IMO number, AIS track history, flag state and insurance cover) proving no port call in restricted jurisdictions; OFAC/EU/UN sanction-list screening reports for every counterparty, beneficial owner, and bank (with screenshots and timestamp); contractual origin and anti-transhipment clauses under current ICC rules; distinct self-attestations from all counterparties; and a written sanctions-compliance manual approved by a French avocat specialising in EU restrictive measures. Any blocked-party name must be rejected outright.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Misclassification as a payment or money-transmission business: recurring pass-through of freight, demurrage, or hull insurance premiums could be mis-characterised by the bank's KYC engine as payment-services activity requiring an ACPR licence as an établissement de paiement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISIC 4631 / French NAF 4621Z business plan; agency and brokerage mandate under French commercial law (contrat de commissionnaire) explicit that the SARL acts as market intermediary for the account of principals and never takes possession of grain or funds belonging to third parties; copies of commission invoices (facture d'apporteur d'affaires) showing remuneration as a margin rather than a flat fee on fund movement; accountant's letter confirming the transaction flow is not subject to the Code Monétaire et Financier, Article L.521-1; entity classification declaration on the ACPR single-portal if any doubt remains.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP and adverse-media flags affecting a counterparty or a non-resident shareholder with a government-linked agricultural export background.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP self-certification forms for all officers and UBOs; negative-media reports from World-Check or equivalent (dated and saved); independent legal opinion confirming the counterparty is not acting in a public-official capacity in the transaction; enhanced due diligence file on the final grain importer including ultimate-owner passports, licensing by the destination-ministry of agriculture, and where available, a confirming bank's endorsement on the LC.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant structure: (i) Equity subscription — SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA debit/credit transfer for smaller amounts) from the shareholder's bank to the SARL's blocked account (compte bloqué) at the incorporation bank; Field 50F/T bank-and-client details, Field 70 must recite: 'Souscription au capital social - SARL [name] - SIREN [xxx] - Article L.223-7 du Code de commerce' together with the statutory Banque de France BOP purpose indicator for direct investment (capital creation). A French SARL has no statutory minimum capital, but capitalising at EUR 10,000-50,000 is strongly advised to satisfy bank viability and to evidence commercial substance. (ii) Shareholder loan (compte courant d'associé) — executed loan deed dated before or simultaneously with the transfer; declared in the annual information statement for BOP statistical purposes; interest deductible only within the cap set under Article 39-1-3° of the Code Général des Impôts (annual ministerial rate), with 10-year maximum pre-amortisation period to avoid deemed dividend requalification; bank Field 70 must identify 'Prêt d'actionnaire — convention du [date]'. (iii) Verification step: the bank will match the inbound wire to the declared purpose code; any mismatch is reported to TRACFIN under suspicion-based reporting; therefore the SARL must keep the deed, board resolution, and bank references identical. Cash contributions above EUR 10,000 are prohibited at the border and impractical in banking onboarding; all capital movements must be executed via the banking trail.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail — Irrevocable Transferable Letter of Credit issued in USD or EUR governed by UCP 600: the issuing bank (overseas importer's bank or a French confirming bank for a two-leg structure) transmits SWIFT MT700 / MT707; the SARL appears as first beneficiary and transfers a compliant portion to the grain or vessel supplier, preserving its margin; proceeds discounted by the confirming bank into the SARL's operational account. Secondary rail — SWIFT MT103/TT wires for freight, demurrage, insurance, surveyor fees, and genuine open-account settlements: each MT103 must include the ISO 20022-compatible UETR (Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference), Field 71A charges rules, and an unambiguous structured remittance descriptor (e.g., 'Demurrage - vessel M/V [name] - B/L [number] - fixture [ID]'). Trade-rail matching requires the three-document equality test at the bank: Invoice value = LC drawing amount = B/L quantity × contracted unit price; where the SARL acts as broker, booking and settlement must be handled on a principal-to-principal basis with separate commission invoicing to avoid redirection red flags. Retention of all underlying documents for five years is mandatory under French tax and customs rules and for TRACFIN on-demand production.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD delivery forwards (change à terme, maturities 1-12 months) with any ACPR-licensed credit institution, directly covering grain sale proceeds, vessel costs, or LC disbursements denominated in USD
Window and deferred-start forwards staggered against laycan/demurrage schedules to nullify settlement-date basis risk in charter payments

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on EUR/BRL and EUR/ARS for Brazilian soybean and Argentine corn/meal origins, executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or the FBF (Fédération Bancaire Française) FX Master Agreement, evidenced by a physical underlying cargo contract
Cross-currency swaps (swap de change) and short-tenor collateralised FX swaps to bridge USD payables against EUR treasury surplus without transforming the balance sheet

Plain vanilla EUR/USD currency options and zero-cost collars (collar de change) enabling the SARL to preserve upside participation while protecting a minimum net margin during seasonal grain price rallies

Commodity-embedded FX structures limited to professional counterparties, including EUR/USD quanto swaps and price-indexed FX swaps linked to CBOT/Euronext futures, provided they are demonstrably hedging physical grain flows and are not speculative in nature

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual financial statements (comptes annuels: balance sheet, profit & loss, annexes) with the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS dossier) via formalite.entreprises.gouv.fr
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must approve accounts within 6 months of fiscal year-end; the approved accounts must be filed with the registry within 1 month after approval and no later than 7 months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty up to EUR 7,500 for the legal representative; the registry may issue a formal enforcement notice and the court may order the filing under a coercive fine; prolonged non-compliance can trigger administrative strike-off from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' general meeting decision approving the financial statements and appropriation of profits
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records maintained at the registered office; minutes recorded in the company's decision register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least one meeting each calendar year, within 6 months of the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Any partner may require the managing director to call a meeting; persistent failure may constitute serious mismanagement and a partner may apply to the court for dissolution after more than 2 consecutive missed meetings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership declaration (Déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs) filed with the annual accounts or updated upon any change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; transmitted to the Ministry of Justice beneficial ownership register (RBO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial declaration within 15 days of creation; annual declaration filed together with the annual accounts; any change in beneficial ownership must be declared within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to EUR 37,500 and/or imprisonment up to 6 months for intent to conceal beneficial owners; registry may refuse to file accounts until the declaration is rectified

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Déclaration de résultats: IS/2065 for profits, with balance sheet and annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) - online e-filing for commercial companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year ending 31 December: electronic filing due by 3 May; the deadline is extended to 15 May for online-filed returns; for truncated year-ends, filing is due within 3 months of year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of assessed corporate income tax plus late-payment interest at 0.2% per month; an additional 40% penalty applies for knowing or deliberate omissions; failure to file may trigger an automatic assessment and, for repeated non-compliance, criminal sanction

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit (commissaire aux comptes) applies where, at fiscal year-end, the SARL exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds: EUR 4,000,000 total assets, EUR 8,000,000 net turnover, and 50 employees. Appointed auditor terms are six years (or up to ten years for listed-like mandates).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Règlement ANC 2014-03, Plan Comptable Général) is mandatory for statutory French accounts; optional IFRS applies for consolidated financial statements of listed groups or where EU/Commission permits. The entity is within the statutory French accounting regime.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The beneficial owner declaration is an annual filing that accompanies the first submission of accounts. For subsequent years, no standalone annual UBO recertification is required unless there is a shareholding transfer or other change in beneficial ownership; within 30 days of any such transfer, the updated declaration must be filed. The registry also expects a practical confirmation in the annual corporate secretarial questionnaire that the on-file UBO register remains truthful.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Share Transfers (registre de mouvements de titres)
Register of Deliberative Assembly Decisions (registre des décisions et minutes)
Register of Beneficial Owners (when physically maintained; otherwise filed declaration is the register)
